lessons.title: HTTP Cache-Control & Stale-While-Revalidate Mechanisms
lessons.content:
### HTTP Cache-Control & Stale-While-Revalidate Mechanisms

Optimizing web delivery latency requires deep mastery of modern caching directives. The `stale-while-revalidate` (SWR) directive bridges instantaneous client rendering with asynchronous cache warming.

#### Cache Directive Hierarchy
- `public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=86400`: Deliver from edge cache instantly for 60 seconds; serve stale cached content for up to 24 hours while revalidating against origin in the background.
- `immutable`: Informs user agents that responses with content-hashed assets will never mutate.
- `no-cache`: Forces cache validation with `ETag` or `If-Modified-Since` headers prior to reuse.

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: public, max-age=120, stale-while-revalidate=3600
ETag: W/"33a64df551425fcc55e4d42a148795d9f25f89d4"
Vary: Accept-Encoding
```

#### Edge Compute Interception Pattern
Edge workers (Cloudflare Workers, Fastly Compute, AWS Lambda@Edge) allow processing authentication and localized rendering milliseconds away from the client.

quiz.title: Certification Examination: Distributed Web Systems Architecture

questions.text: In a Webpack Module Federation setup, what is the consequence of configuring a shared library with 'singleton: true' when two remotes require conflicting major versions?
options: The host fails to boot and produces a fatal Webpack compilation error.
A runtime warning is emitted, and the highest compatible or host-loaded version is used across all remotes.
Each remote automatically clones and injects its own version into a separate JavaScript realm.
The browser initiates a synchronous fetch to re-bundle the dependency tree at runtime.
questions.explanation: When singleton: true is defined, Module Federation permits only one instance of the library in the shared scope. If versions are incompatible according to semantic version constraints, a runtime warning is logged and the highest loaded instance is reused to prevent multiple React/DOM reconciler instances.

questions.text: Under what engineering circumstance is Server-Sent Events (SSE) objectively preferable over WebSockets?
options: When high-frequency binary data packets (such as audio streams) must be transmitted in full duplex.
When communication is unidirectional from server to client, requiring native auto-reconnection and seamless HTTP/2 multiplexing through corporate firewalls.
When peer-to-peer UDP packet transmission is mandated by strict real-time gaming latencies.
When the client needs to initiate frequent RPC requests across the same underlying persistent socket.
questions.explanation: SSE operates over standard HTTP, natively benefits from HTTP/2 multiplexing, traverses corporate firewalls without special TCP socket upgrades, and includes built-in browser automatic reconnection with message ID tracking.

questions.text: What does the 'stale-while-revalidate' directive instruct an edge CDN or browser cache to perform?
options: Immediately purge stale items from memory and force the browser to display a loading skeleton until origin responds.
Return cached assets immediately while asynchronously dispatching a revalidation request to update the cache for subsequent requests.
Permanently cache the response on disk until the user manually triggers a hard browser reload.
Compress all outgoing payloads with Brotli encoding before evaluating the ETag header.
questions.explanation: Stale-While-Revalidate allows the cache to respond immediately with stale content within a defined window, while initiating an asynchronous revalidation request to refresh the cache in the background.

questions.text: When decoupling micro-frontends on a single page, which architectural approach provides the cleanest isolation and boundary defense?
options: Binding state directly to 'window.globalState' and letting all remotes mutate properties directly.
Employing a strongly typed Event Broker or CustomEvent bus with immutable payloads and localized error boundaries.
Importing the host application root component directly into every individual remote bundle.
Executing each remote inside an invisible iframe with postMessage serialization for every DOM event.
questions.explanation: A strongly typed event broker or CustomEvent bus provides loose coupling, decouples deployment dependencies, enforces immutable message payloads, and preserves native DOM rendering performance without iframe overhead.

lessons.title: Generational Garbage Collection: Scavenger vs Major Mark-Sweep
lessons.content:
### Generational Garbage Collection: Scavenger vs Major Mark-Sweep

V8 partitions heap memory based on the **Generational Hypothesis**: most objects die young.

- **New Space (Nursery)**: Managed by the Minor GC (Scavenger). Operates via Cheney's copying algorithm with fast allocation pointers.
- **Old Space**: Stores long-lived objects promoted after surviving two GC cycles. Managed by Major GC (Mark-Sweep-Compact).
- **WeakRef & FinalizationRegistry**: Allows safe tracking of garbage-collected objects without preventing their deallocation.

questions.text: What happens when microtasks continuously enqueue additional microtasks during a single event loop turn?
options: The browser forcibly pauses the microtask queue after 16 milliseconds to yield to paint frames.
The event loop drains all newly enqueued microtasks consecutively, blocking UI rendering and starving macrotasks.
Microtasks are converted automatically into macrotasks scheduled on the next iteration.
A RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded exception is thrown immediately.
questions.explanation: According to the HTML specification, the microtask checkpoint does not exit until the microtask queue is completely empty. If microtasks perpetually enqueue more microtasks, the event loop starves UI rendering, user interaction, and all macrotasks.

questions.text: How does V8's TurboFan compiler handle a function if an object parameter exhibits differing internal shapes (Polymorphism) across calls?
options: It re-allocates contiguous memory arrays on every single invocation.
It downgrades the inline cache to a megamorphic stub or triggers deoptimization back to Ignition bytecode.
It executes WebAssembly ahead-of-time compilation to bypass object lookups.
It permanently deletes the function from memory and raises an UncaughtTypeError.
questions.explanation: Inline Caches (IC) optimize based on monomorphic assumptions. When object shapes vary beyond 4 different variants, the IC transitions to megamorphic, disabling speculative inlining and deoptimizing back to interpreted bytecode.

questions.text: Which memory heap space in V8 is responsible for holding ephemeral short-lived objects using a fast copying collector?
options: Old Pointer Space
Large Object Space
New Space (Young Generation)
Code Space (Executable JIT memory)
questions.explanation: New Space (or Young Generation) is divided into two semi-spaces managed by the Scavenger collector. It allocates ephemeral objects rapidly and moves survivors to the Old Space upon surviving generational GC cycles.

questions.text: Which statement accurately describes the behavior of WeakMap keys in JavaScript?
options: Keys can be arbitrary primitives or strings, which are automatically cleared on browser refresh.
Keys must be objects or non-registered symbols, allowing them to be garbage collected when no other strong references exist.
Keys are enumerable through Object.keys() only when the inspector devtools are attached.
Keys retain strong references until the WeakMap instance is explicitly destroyed with delete().
questions.explanation: WeakMap keys must be garbage-collectable values (objects or non-registered symbols). They do not create strong references, allowing the garbage collector to reclaim the key and value once external references cease.

questions.text: How do CSS Cascade Layers (@layer) resolve conflicting rules between two different layers when selector specificity differs?
options: The rule with the highest individual selector specificity wins regardless of layer ordering.
The layer defined later in the layer declaration sequence always takes precedence for normal declarations, regardless of selector specificity.
The browser concatenates styles and applies CSS animation keyframes across both selectors.
Layers with ID selectors override all other layers unconditionally.
questions.explanation: In CSS Cascade Layers, layer order takes precedence over selector specificity. Normal declarations inside a later-declared layer will defeat declarations from an earlier layer, even if the earlier layer used a much higher-specificity selector.

questions.text: What property must be declared on a parent element to establish a container query context based on its width?
options: contain: content layout;
container-type: inline-size;
display: container-flex;
content-visibility: auto;
questions.explanation: container-type: inline-size creates a containment context that monitors the element's inline axis (width in horizontal writing modes), allowing child elements to target it with @container queries.

questions.text: What is the primary benefit of a 3-tier token hierarchy (Primitive -> Semantic -> Component) in CSS?
options: It decreases total HTTP transfer size by 90% via Gzip dictionary duplication.
It decouples raw brand colors from interface intent, enabling global theme switching without touching component stylesheets.
It enables client-side WebAssembly execution for all DOM mutations.
It converts all CSS declarations to static SVG vector files at build time.
questions.explanation: Decoupling raw values into semantic tokens allows centralized theming (such as light/dark mode and high-contrast modes) while isolating component styling from branding changes.

questions.text: Which CSS properties trigger GPU hardware acceleration without causing CPU-bound layout recalculations or repaints?
options: width, height, top, left
transform and opacity
margin, padding, border-width
box-shadow, color, background-color
questions.explanation: transform and opacity are handled directly during the GPU compositing phase without recalculating DOM layout (reflow) or repainting pixels, making them ideal for high-performance 60fps animations.

lessons.title: Subresource Integrity (SRI) Cryptographic Pinning
lessons.content:
### Subresource Integrity (SRI) Cryptographic Pinning

Loading third-party assets from CDNs opens web platforms to supply chain compromise. If an attacker compromises the external CDN, they can deliver arbitrary malicious JavaScript directly into your users' active sessions.

Subresource Integrity ensures the user agent validates that fetched files match a pre-calculated cryptographic hash before executing them.

```html
<script 
  src="https://cdn.devpath.io/vendor/crypto-utils.min.js"
  integrity="sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC"
  crossorigin="anonymous">
</script>
```

quiz.title: Certification Examination: Web Application Security Engineering

questions.text: Why is storing sensitive session JWTs inside window.localStorage considered a severe security vulnerability?
options: LocalStorage data is automatically flushed when the user closes their browser tab.
Any injected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) payload can access and exfiltrate window.localStorage without restriction.
LocalStorage requests bypass SSL/TLS encryption across the local network.
LocalStorage values can be read by any external domain on the public internet.
questions.explanation: LocalStorage is directly accessible to any JavaScript executing in the same origin context. If an application suffers from an XSS vulnerability, an attacker can extract all tokens stored in localStorage. HttpOnly cookies prevent JavaScript DOM access entirely.

questions.text: What protection is conferred by the '__Host-' cookie prefix?
options: It automatically rotates the cookie value every 60 seconds using DNS over HTTPS.
The browser ensures the cookie must be Secure, have Path=/, and can only be set from the exact origin without subdomain inheritance.
It permits the cookie to be shared across completely distinct top-level domains.
It turns off cookie compression to prevent BREACH attacks.
questions.explanation: The __Host- prefix tells browsers to accept the cookie only if it includes Secure, Path=/, and is set from the host itself without domain attributes, shielding against subdomain cookie hijacking.

questions.text: What is the primary role of Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) in OAuth 2.1?
options: It acts as a substitute for HTTPS encryption across untrusted Wi-Fi networks.
It prevents malicious authorization code injection and interception on public clients that cannot securely store client secrets.
It generates one-time passwords for biometric hardware keys.
It automatically generates Content Security Policy headers on the client.
questions.explanation: PKCE dynamically creates a cryptographic code_verifier and code_challenge pair, ensuring that only the original client who initiated the authorization request can exchange the returned authorization code for access tokens.

questions.text: What will happen if a script loaded with an 'integrity' attribute fails the cryptographic hash check against the downloaded content?
options: The browser executes the script in sandboxed mode and suppresses network calls.
The browser refuses to execute the script and triggers an error event on the element.
The browser prompts the user with an interactive dialog asking for confirmation.
The browser falls back to loading the file without integrity enforcement.
questions.explanation: Subresource Integrity blocks execution immediately and emits an error event if the SHA hash of the fetched asset does not strictly match the expected integrity value specified in the tag.
